chunks: And in the narration of al-Mu‘allā ibn Khunays, from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
I asked him about a woman who prays in a dir‘ and a milḥafah, with no izār or miqna‘ah upon her.
He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm if she wraps herself in it, and if it is not sufficient for her in width, she should make it lengthwise.”

key_terms.إِزَارٌ: a waistcloth or lower wrap garment
key_terms.دِرْعٍ: a shift or long shirt worn as a garment
key_terms.عَرْضًا: in width, meaning the breadth of the garment
key_terms.مِلْحَفَةٍ: a wrapping cover or outer cloth
key_terms.ٱلْتَفَّتْ: wrapped herself properly in the cloth
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْأَةِ: the woman in question regarding the ruling of salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Can a woman perform salat (prayer) in a dir‘ and milḥafah without an izār or miqna‘ah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a woman’s dress in salat (prayer), indicating that prayer is valid if she wraps herself properly in the garment mentioned. If the cloth is not wide enough, she may arrange it lengthwise to achieve sufficient coverage.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1084 - In a narration from Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays,
he asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about a woman praying in a shirt (dir') and a cover (milhafa) without a waistcloth (izar) or headcover (miqna'a).
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm if She wraps herself in it, and if it is not wide enough to cover her, She should make it long."
